landingPage.title: Survey Designer
landingPage.description:
Welcome to Survey Designer! This tool allows you to build 
 high-quality, multi-lingual, standardized surveys in a few 
 simple steps. It follows the WFP standard naming conventions 
 (Codebook) while giving you flexibility on what to include in 
 your survey. It allows you to either generate the survey as an 
 XLSForm or to push directly into ODK-based tools such as: MoDa 
 and Kobo.

surveyDesigner.question: What is Survey Designer?
surveyDesigner.paragraph1: Survey Designer is an application that allows users in the field to build surveys in a fast and easy way while also giving them the flexibility to make necessary adjustments, all while maintaining WFP standard labeling and naming conventions based on the WFP Codebook and standard list of questions and answers. This improves overall data quality for survey design, data collection, and analysis by saving time and resources, while also allowing reproducibility and resource sharing between users. This tool is targeted to users working with XLSForm or ODK-based tools such as MoDa or Kobo.

codebook.question: What is the Codebook?
codebook.paragraph1: The WFP <codebook>Codebook</codebook> is a dataset containing all possible standard questions and answers included in WFP surveys.
codebook.paragraph2: It is linked to an XLSForm database that can be subject to integrations and revisions based on data collection needs.
codebook.paragraph4: The <codebook>Codebook</codebook> in Survey Designer cannot be directly modified, but there is a <requestChangeProcedure>Request Change Procedure</requestChangeProcedure> that allows you to propose modifications to the administrators.

categoriesTypesModesContext.question: What are Survey Categories, Types, Modes and Context?
categoriesTypesModesContext.paragraph1: These are filters that you can use to structure or define your survey.
categoriesTypesModesContext.paragraph2: Based on your choices, different submodules of questions are included in your survey.
categoriesTypesModesContext.paragraph3: <surveyCategories>Survey Categories</surveyCategories> are general macro-categories, currently Monitoring, Market, and Vulnerability Assessments, that define your survey.
categoriesTypesModesContext.paragraph4: <surveyTypes>Survey Types</surveyTypes> are sub-categories specific to each category you select, for example for Monitoring you have PDM, Baseline Monitoring, and others.
categoriesTypesModesContext.paragraph5: <surveyModes>Survey Modes</surveyModes> are the three data collection modes allowed for WFP surveys: Face-to-face, Remote/CATI, and Web Surveys.
categoriesTypesModesContext.paragraph6: <context>Context</context> consists of additional sets of questions that can be optionally added to specific modules, for example COVID-19-related questions or migration-related questions.

modulesSubmodules.question: What are Modules and Submodules?
modulesSubmodules.paragraph1: <modules>Modules</modules> and <submodules>Submodules</submodules>, sometimes also referred to as sections, are a way to group questions based on thematic areas such as Nutrition or Food Security, and on how they are normally grouped in surveys.
modulesSubmodules.paragraph2: They are organized and labelled based on standard WFP Codebook conventions.
modulesSubmodules.paragraph3: <submodules>Submodules</submodules> are the basic unit that you will use to create a survey in Survey Designer.

suffixesRecallPeriods.question: What are Suffixes and Recall Periods?
suffixesRecallPeriods.paragraph1: In the Codebook, each question may have several optional variations.
suffixesRecallPeriods.paragraph2: For every question, we identify a Root Question, which expresses the basic corporate formulation of a question.
suffixesRecallPeriods.paragraph3: Suffixes indicate logic variations of the Root Question. For example, Root Question HHExpFood is read as "What is your total food expenditure?" If we add the suffix _Loc, which is related to locations, we obtain the subquestion HHExpFood_Loc, read as "Where do you purchase your food?" The Codebook allows up to a maximum of two suffixes for a single subquestion. In that case, the second suffix is called a nested suffix.
suffixesRecallPeriods.paragraph4: Recall Periods indicate the time reference for a question. For example, if we add the recall period _7D, indicating a weekly time reference, we obtain the subquestion HHExpFood_7D, read as "What was your total food expenditure in the last 7 days?"
suffixesRecallPeriods.paragraph5: Suffixes and Recall Periods can also be combined to create subquestions that are both logic and temporal variations of the Root Question. For example, HHExpFood_Loc_7D is read as "Where did you purchase your food in the last 7 days?"

calculationsRepeatSections.question: What are Calculations and Repeat Sections?
calculationsRepeatSections.paragraph1: <calculations>Calculations</calculations> and <repeatSections>Repeat Sections</repeatSections> are elements that structure your survey but do not necessarily appear in the final questionnaire.
calculationsRepeatSections.paragraph2: <calculations>Calculations</calculations> produce standard calculations, such as aggregations or indicator scores, based on collected data. Those calculations may appear in the survey or not, depending on your decision.
calculationsRepeatSections.paragraph3: <repeatSections>Repeat Sections</repeatSections> define how a set of questions is repeated in the survey based on specific information, for example asking about the age and sex of each household member based on household size.

buildSurvey.question: How do I build a survey using Survey Designer?
buildSurvey.paragraph1: We have a tailored step-by-step guide and an online recording that explain the process.
buildSurvey.paragraph2: If you have more questions, please email us at <supportEmail>global.surveydesigner@wfp.org</supportEmail>.

surveyTypes.question: What kind of surveys can I build using Survey Designer?
surveyTypes.paragraph1: Survey Designer allows you to build any standard WFP survey that has been integrated into the Codebook.
surveyTypes.paragraph2: You may view the available standard WFP surveys by viewing <surveyCategories>Survey Categories</surveyCategories> and <surveyTypes>Types</surveyTypes>.
surveyTypes.paragraph3: If you want to access all available WFP questions and answers, do not select a specific Category, Type, Mode, or Attribute. You can then create any type of non-standard survey by combining the modules and submodules that you need.
surveyTypes.paragraph4: If the modules or submodules required by your business unit are not included in the Codebook, please email <supportEmail>global.surveydesigner@wfp.org</supportEmail> and we will guide you through the addition request process.

exportPublish.question: What are the options for exporting or publishing surveys?
exportPublish.paragraph1: Currently, Survey Designer allows you to export your survey as an XLSForm, or directly publish it into <moda>MoDa</moda> or <kobo>Kobo</kobo>.
exportPublish.paragraph2: To publish into <moda>MoDa</moda> or <kobo>Kobo</kobo>, you need to enter your API key for each site <apiKeysPage>here</apiKeysPage>.

selectionLimit.question: Is there a limit to the modules or questions that I can select?
selectionLimit.paragraph1: No, you can add as many modules or questions as you need in a survey.

accessCodebook.question: How can I access the Codebook?
accessCodebook.paragraph1: You can access the <codebook>Codebook</codebook> by clicking the "<codebook>Codebook</codebook>" button at the top right next to your username.
accessCodebook.paragraph2: From there you can access all the back-end content that contributes to building surveys, including Questions, Answers, Suffixes, Calculations, Survey Categories, Types, Modes, and others.

exportExcel.question: Can I export the Codebook content in Excel format?
exportExcel.paragraph1: Yes. You can export Codebook content in Excel format by selecting one or more <modules>Modules</modules>, <submodules>Submodules</submodules>, or <questions>Questions</questions>, then clicking the "Export Questions" action button.

contributeChanges.question: How can I contribute to the Codebook (request addition or changes)?
contributeChanges.paragraph1: You can submit requests to add, edit, or delete questions or answers by accessing <submitChangeRequest>this link</submitChangeRequest>.
contributeChanges.paragraph2: Alternatively, you may send your request to <supportEmail>global.surveydesigner@wfp.org</supportEmail> and attach an Excel sheet with the required changes.

contact.title: Contact Survey Designer Team
contact.paragraph1: If you have any queries or you would like to report any bugs, please email <supportEmail>global.surveydesigner@wfp.org</supportEmail>.
